transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time. I came in because I’ve just been feeling really tired all the time. I mean, I know being a teacher means you're always a little exhausted by the end of the day, so I feel a little silly bringing it up, but it feels different than just normal work stress? 

Like, even after a really good, full night’s sleep, I still have to just... force myself to push through grading my students' papers, and then making dinner, and getting everything ready for the next morning. I really try not to complain, but it's just been a bit of a struggle lately. Does that make sense? Is that okay to come in for?
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so? I still really love my job, and my students are wonderful. And I still enjoy, you know, reading or baking on the weekends. I definitely still *want* to do things. 

It's really just... the energy to actually start them is what's missing, I guess? But I definitely still enjoy my hobbies once I'm doing them! I hope that makes sense? I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around miserable or anything, because I'm really not. I have a very good life, and I'm very grateful for it. Is it okay if it's mostly just the tiredness?
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless at any point during the day or week?

Oh, definitely not hopeless! I really don't want to sound ungrateful or dramatic. Um... and sad might even be a little too strong of a word? 

I mean, most days I can absolutely still smile for my students, and I get through all the lessons just fine. I always make sure they see a happy face, you know? But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, underneath it all, there's just this... sort of gray, flat feeling? It just kind of quietly follows me home at the end of the day. And when I'm back at the house, that flat feeling just makes everything—even my garden or my watercolors—seem kind of... far away? Like I'm just a little disconnected from it all. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit contradictory to what I just said about still enjoying my hobbies. I hope I'm explaining it right. Does that make sense to feel that way?
Have you found yourself feeling more critical of yourself lately, or maybe feeling like you're not good enough or don't measure up?

Oh, um... well, I really try not to be too hard on myself, because I know everyone has their struggles. And I certainly don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or anything. But... I guess, maybe a little bit? 

I just... I keep thinking I should be handling everything better. Like, I'm a professional, I've been doing this for a while, you know? But lately, my lesson plans are taking me twice as long to get through because I just can't focus, and... well, the other day I actually had to say no to mentoring one of the newer teachers. Which is terrible, because I love helping out! And when things like that happen, I just... I kind of tell myself I'm letting my school down, and my students, and even my family because I'm just so drained when I get home. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably silly to get so worked up over. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for everyone. Is it normal to feel guilty about things like that?
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

Oh, um... well, I know I just mentioned that thing about my lesson plans taking a bit longer, but... I really don't think it's a problem with my actual thinking or making decisions? I definitely don't want you to worry that I'm not capable in the classroom or anything like that. 

When I'm actually teaching the kids, my mind is completely clear, and I can make all those split-second decisions just fine. I'm still very organized, I promise! It's really just... maybe when I'm sitting alone at my desk at the end of the day and that tired feeling creeps in, my mind just wanders a little bit? So I might have to re-read a paragraph here or there. But my memory and my ability to think things through are still perfectly fine. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to be clear that I'm still doing my job well and keeping on top of things. I'm not losing my edge or anything, I promise.
Have you experienced a depressed mood — like feeling sad, empty, or tearful — most of the day, nearly every day, even if it's subtle or easy to overlook?

Oh, um... well, I know we touched on this a little bit earlier, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much. I definitely wouldn't say I'm tearful, and I'm not sitting around crying all day, I promise! I don't want to give the impression that I'm falling apart. 

Like I said before, most days I can absolutely still smile for my students, and I get through all the lessons just fine. I think I do a really good job of keeping things upbeat for them. But... yes, I guess if I'm being completely honest, underneath it all, there is just that... that gray, flat feeling I mentioned. It just kind of quietly follows me home, and it makes the things I usually love—like my garden or my watercolors—just feel a bit... far away? Like I'm going through the motions. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm kind of saying the same thing again. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. Does that count as what you're asking about?
Can you think of a time recently when you genuinely looked forward to doing something, like a hobby or seeing friends? Did it feel as rewarding as it used to?

Oh, um... well, I really do try to stay active and engaged, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing! I still see my friends, and I still get out. 

But... oh gosh, I don't know if I can pinpoint a specific time recently where I felt that really big, exciting anticipation? I mean, I still enjoy things, of course! We had a staff luncheon last week and it was lovely to chat with everyone. I just... I guess maybe the feeling of looking forward to it wasn't as strong as it used to be? It felt a little more like... like something I was supposed to do, rather than something I couldn't wait for. 

And my hobbies... well, I still do my watercolors when I can, but I suppose the satisfaction at the end of a painting isn't quite as bright as it once was. It's still nice, though! I'm definitely not giving up on the things I like. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just don't want to sound ungrateful for the good things in my life, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. Is it okay that the excitement is just... a little muted right now?

Oh, um... well, I mean, teaching is naturally an exhausting job, right? So I really try not to complain about being tired. I know everyone gets tired! But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, that is actually the main reason I finally decided to make an appointment to see you. 

I just... I feel tired all the time lately. And I know what the normal "teacher-at-the-end-of-the-day" tired feels like, I'm very used to that! But this feels a little different? It's like, even if I get a really good, full night's sleep, I still have to really, really push myself just to get through my grading, make dinner, and get my classroom things ready for the next morning. 

I'm still getting it all done, I promise! I never skip my prep or let things slide at home. It just takes a lot more effort to push through it than it usually does, I think? I hope it's okay that I'm bringing that up, I don't want to sound like a complainer. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Does that make sense?

I'm definitely still putting in the effort! I hope that's an okay answer?
